videos.title: The Easy Habit That Sets Your Mood For The Day | Dr. Andrew Huberman
videos.description:
Dopamine was never the feel-good chemical. It’s the reason you keep reaching for the next thing, and the reason the crash after it keeps getting deeper.

In this clip, Andrew Huberman and Jay Shetty talk about the two things your brain needs before it can learn anything, and why one of them is doing nothing at all.

Andrew explains what actually happens in your brain while you sleep, why the small things feel enormous when you’re tired, and what a study on college students camping for two nights says about the clock inside every cell in your body.

Learn about the brain area people chose to stimulate more than any other, why missing someone is a good sign, and the one habit Andrew would give every person on earth.

JAY’S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

videos.title: You don't have to review every AI-generated PR
videos.description: Merge Mommy doesn't actually merge PRs. It posts a gray check in GitHub (a signal, not an approval), then pings my colleague and me in Slack with the risk score and a note that says "you can approve and merge." That two-click handoff keeps a human accountable for the merge action while removing all the cognitive overhead of actually reviewing the code.
